transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Uh… mostly I’m here because I can’t sit still. Like in the radiology suite, or in class, it feels like I’m crawling out of my skin if I’m supposed to stay put. I’ve tried to just deal with it for months, but I still end up pacing, shifting around, or making some excuse to move.
Did this feeling of not being able to sit still start after you began taking a medication or changed the dose of one?
I don’t think so. I mean… I haven’t really connected it to any medication change or anything like that.
Did you often feel this same kind of restlessness when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. My parents still bring up those elementary school conferences where teachers said I was always out of my seat, calling out, or rushing ahead before they finished directions. So… it was definitely before middle school, not just since the radiology training.
Do you have unwanted thoughts that keep coming into your mind and feel hard to ignore?
Um… not really. I mean, I get distracted and stuff, but I don’t think I have thoughts that feel like they’re forcing their way in or anything.
Do you often make careless mistakes because it’s hard to keep your attention on details?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I make mistakes sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s because of details specifically.
Do you often feel excessively worried, even when there isn’t a clear reason to be?
I don’t know… not really excessively, I guess. I worry about normal stuff, but I wouldn’t say it comes out of nowhere all the time.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task, even when you want to pay attention?
Yeah… I guess sometimes. It kind of depends on the task. I can try to pay attention, but my mind doesn’t always stay there.
When you were in school as a child, did you often have trouble finishing assignments?
I’m not sure. I mean, I think I finished most things eventually, but I don’t really remember if it was a big problem back then.
Do you often interrupt other people or blurt out answers before they finish speaking?
Yeah… I do that. Like if my supervisor is explaining a positioning step, I’ll jump in before they’re done, thinking I know the answer. Then I realize I missed the part that actually mattered.
When you have trouble sitting still, does it feel like an inner urge to keep moving?

Yeah. It’s like… I don’t know, I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin when I’m supposed to just sit there, like in class or in the radiology suite. I try to tough it out, but I end up shifting around, pacing, or finding some reason to get up.
Do you often feel driven to be active or on the go, even in situations where other people seem able to relax?
Yeah… pretty much. Most days I’m going from class to clinicals, then the gym or errands, and if I have free time I usually fill it with something. Just sitting around feels really hard.
Are you currently taking, or have you recently taken, any medication like an antipsychotic or nausea medicine such as metoclopramide?
Um… not that I know of. I don’t think I’m on anything like that.
Do you often get distracted easily in your day-to-day activities?
I mean… I’m not really sure. I guess I can get sidetracked sometimes, but I haven’t really paid close attention to that.
Do you often have difficulty organizing tasks and activities?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. I kind of just do things as they come up. I haven’t really thought about whether it’s an organizing problem.
Do you often avoid tasks that require sustained mental effort?
I’m not sure… I mean, I don’t really think about it that way. If something feels like it’s gonna take a lot of focus, I might put it off, but I don’t know if I’d say I “often” avoid it.
Do you often have trouble waiting your turn?

Yeah… I think so. Like in lab, if I’m waiting for a machine or for my turn to practice, I get really edgy. I’ll keep moving up, checking the time, asking if I can go next… I’ve been called out for it a couple times.
Outside of class or clinicals, does this restlessness cause problems for you in other parts of your life?

Yeah… it does. Not just in class. Like, if I’m supposed to be sitting still in the radiology suite or even just waiting around, I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I try to just deal with it, but I end up pacing or shifting around, or making some excuse to get up and move.
Do you often have trouble following through on instructions and finishing tasks?
I don’t know… not really sure. I mean, sometimes I don’t finish stuff right away, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s because of instructions or anything.
When you feel unable to sit still, does it usually happen because you feel anxious or nervous?

Not really anxious, no. It’s more like… I just can’t settle. If I’m supposed to sit still in the radiology suite or classroom, I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin, and I end up shifting around or finding some reason to get up.
When you get up and move around, does that relieve the uncomfortable feeling?
Yeah… a little. Getting up helps for the moment, I guess. If I can pace or shift around, it takes the edge off that crawling-out-of-my-skin feeling, but it doesn’t really go away for long.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly hyperactive/impulsive symptoms, with onset in childhood and persistence into current academic/clinical settings. The patient confirms longstanding hyperactivity/impulsivity symptoms before middle school, including being out of seat, calling out, rushing ahead, interrupting, difficulty waiting turn, and feeling driven to be active. Functional impairment is present in class, clinical training, and daily life. Akathisia was considered because of the inner restlessness and relief with movement, but is less likely given no antipsychotic/metoclopramide exposure or medication change and clear childhood onset. Anxiety disorder is less likely because the patient denies excessive anxiety as the driver of the restlessness.
